label: OpenAI

disputes.what: OpenAI's 2015 launch post named Peter Thiel among funders who had committed money. TechCrunch (17 May 2023) wrote that “there is no record of Peter Thiel providing any funds to OpenAI” and that his venture firm did not reply to its request for information.

note: After its October 2025 restructuring, Microsoft said: “Microsoft holds an investment in OpenAI Group PBC valued at approximately $135 billion, representing roughly 27 percent”; AP reports the nonprofit OpenAI Foundation's stake at about $130 billion. These are valuations, not money paid. OpenAI's own site refused automated reading, so its own figures are not quoted here.

words.quote: Anthropic can’t veto publication, but we can require them to redact information if it falls into predefined categories

disputes.what: ITPro, citing the Financial Times, reported on 9 September 2026 that Anthropic declined to submit Claude Mythos 5.1 to the UK AI Security Institute for testing while granting access to similar US organisations.
disputes.response: Anthropic had not replied to ITPro at publication. A Cabinet Office spokesperson said the institute 'continues to collaborate closely with industry partners, including Anthropic'. Reuters reported on 12 October 2026 that the institute said Anthropic had made clear no organisation outside the US had access to the model.
disputes.source: Anthropic reportedly withholds access to Mythos 5.1 from UK safety testing body (ITPro)

note: Money in, by its own announcements and reporting: venture rounds from a $124 million Series A (2021) to a $65 billion Series H (May 2026); strategic investments from Google and Amazon from 2023, and commitments from Microsoft and NVIDIA (2025); a public offering priced in November 2026, with seven chip and cloud companies agreeing to buy $26 billion of stock alongside it (reported). Its largest investors are also its compute suppliers and sales channels: Leverage Shares, reading the S-1, says “48% of first-half 2026 revenue was sold through cloud marketplaces, which are mainly theirs” (Amazon's and Google's). It also had a $2.5 billion five-year revolving credit line from a bank syndicate (May 2025, reported). On 18 October 2026 it said “5% of Anthropic's shares will be committed today” to a public benefit fund it owns.

label: Google (Google DeepMind)
note: One entry for Google, as some records name the company, for Google DeepMind, and for DeepMind before Google owned it. Each record says which it means. Alphabet funds it from its own revenue: “our 2026 CapEx investments are anticipated to be in the range of $175 to $185 billion” (February 2026; the range was raised later in the year, as reported), and “Alphabet-level activities primarily reflect expenses related to our shared AI research and development” (October 2026). Google acquired DeepMind in 2014; TechCrunch reported “the acquisition price was more than $500 million”, as reported at the time.

label: Meta

disputes.what: The New York Times reported, as relayed by The Daily Beast on 17 October 2026, that Meta took back $25 million of the $65 million it had put into four super PACs: $22 million from the American Technology Excellence Project and $3 million from a California group.
disputes.response: A Meta spokesperson called the refunds “adjustments” and declined to say why, per the same coverage.
disputes.source: Meta Pulls Back $25 Million of Its $65 Million Midterm War Chest (The Daily Beast, citing the New York Times)

note: It funds its AI mainly from its own revenue. Its 2026 capital spending outlook is “in the range of $135-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $130-145 billion” (Meta, 21 October 2026). For its Hyperion data center, “The funds managed by Blue Owl Capital made a cash contribution of approximately $7 billion to the joint venture” (Meta, 21 October 2025).

label: Microsoft
note: It funds its AI mainly from its own revenue. Its chief financial officer said on 28 October 2026 that “for the calendar year, spend should be approximately $170 billion”.

label: xAI
note: Since February 2026 a subsidiary of SpaceX, as reported. SpaceX's own offering “raised $75.0 billion by offering 555.6 million shares at $135” (Renaissance Capital); how much of that reaches xAI is not stated.

label: DeepSeek, Moonshot AI or Z.ai
note: Three separate developers shown as one entry. Each record names the one it concerns; no record here covers all three. Reported funding in 2025 and 2026: for DeepSeek, a round of about 50 billion yuan in which “Founder Liang Wenfeng is committing 20 billion yuan of his own money, a controlling share of the raise” (TNW, citing Reuters); Zhipu AI “has secured 1 billion yuan ($140 million) in fresh funding from Shanghai's state-backed investors” (Caixin, July 2025); Moonshot AI “has reportedly closed a funding round that raised about $3.5 billion” (TechNode, July 2026).
